identification.statement: Treatment was randomly assigned (ratio 0.85), so the per-arm probabilities and their difference given pre-treatment features are experimentally identified intention-to-treat effects. Exposure is not randomized; the complier (exposure) effect in the report is a Wald estimate under the exclusion restriction.

selection.rule: lowest validation pooled log loss (visit + conversion); confirmed on test by paired bootstrap

exposure_complier_effect_wald.assumption: exclusion restriction: eligibility affects outcomes only through exposure
exclusion restriction: eligibility affects outcomes only through exposure

extrapolation_limits: Absolute rates and effect sizes are not representative: Criteo sub-sampled the data non-uniformly so that the true incrementality level cannot be deduced. Use relative structure (ranking, heterogeneity, the correlation of baseline propensity and effect) and re-base with transport() to the world's own rates.
The data pool several incrementality tests of undisclosed advertisers, countries and dates; the population is users reachable by Criteo's display advertising, not a general population.
Features f0..f11 are anonymised random projections with no simulator counterpart; the simulator may use only the response-type table, not the feature-level model.

The effect is the intention-to-treat effect of eligibility for one advertiser's display campaign over one test period (exposure rate among treated users only 3.6%). It does not identify the response to arbitrary ads, prices, content or repeated campaigns, and it says nothing about long-run, carry-over or saturation effects.

No timestamps: no time-based holdout, no dynamics, no seasonality; the holdout is user-level (rows are users) only. Near-duplicate feature vectors occur across rows, so held-out users can resemble training users closely.
transport() assumes each type's treatment effect is a constant odds ratio when the baseline rate changes; this is an assumption, not an estimate.
Visit and conversion are binary per user over the test period; frequency, basket size and revenue are not observed.

post_fit_diagnostics.note: Post-fit diagnostic (not prespecified, does not change the model or its selection). The data pool several incrementality tests whose treatment ratios differ, so treatment is random within a test but slightly associated with the features in the pooled data. Effects conditional on the features (the per-arm models) remain experimentally identified if the features capture test membership; the pooled difference in means is not a valid average effect, and standardised estimates (model-implied, propensity-stratified, IPW) are reported instead.
